assumptions.hypothesis: A core ERP likely serves orders, inventory, purchasing, and accounting, perhaps with modules or adjacent systems.
assumptions.test: Identify actual ERP product, ownership, schemas/modules and data boundaries.

assumptions.hypothesis: B2B webstore likely exchanges customer/product/order data with internal business systems, but sync direction, method and timing are unknown.
assumptions.test: Trace one sample order end-to-end with permission; identify integration endpoints and reconciliation.

assumptions.hypothesis: Warehouse voice-picking data historically moved between ERP and Voxware; current integration and process may have changed.
assumptions.test: Observe present pick/pack/ship workflow and validate current software/vendor state.

assumptions.hypothesis: Sales, purchasing, warehouse, and accounting may use reports with overlapping definitions or manual reconciliation. This is a generic discovery hypothesis, not an allegation of poor data.
assumptions.test: Collect report catalog, lineage, refresh methods, audiences and exceptions with department owners.

assumptions.hypothesis: Shopify may represent a distinct commerce surface or partner integration while the public B2B store uses nopCommerce. The relationship is unknown.
assumptions.test: Ask which web properties or integrations use Shopify and who owns them.

assumptions.hypothesis: Long-tenured operational knowledge, exceptions, and historical decisions could benefit from consented, access-controlled continuity artifacts.
assumptions.test: Ask about transition/handoff pain points; confirm appetite, permissions, retention and sensitivity.

assumptions.hypothesis: Priority sponsorship may sit with operational leadership rather than a conventional software hierarchy.
assumptions.test: Identify hiring manager, budget owner, decision rights and escalation for competing work requests.

assumptions.hypothesis: Use Microsoft SQL Server as the default assumption for all Frontier database instances; Frontier may correct exceptions.
assumptions.test: Ask Frontier to identify exceptions while mapping actual instances, database names, versions and workload ownership.

No nodes or edges were added and no current ERP database or interface was confirmed. Update 2026-11-04: H08 is the single operative SQL Server default for all Frontier database instances. Historical database-unknown notes above remain provenance. No SQL Server instance, common database or production integration edge is invented by this update.

architecture_component_conventions.scope: Frontier business-application and implementation architecture; conversation switch provides its readable register

terminology.Business System: Business operation spanning people, processes, information and technology (example: Transportation / Distribution).
terminology.Business Application: Software product supporting business operations; known/named examples nopCommerce, Voxware and Route4Me; ERP vendor unidentified.
terminology.Business Process: Chronological sequence of business activities (example: Dispatch-to-Delivery).
terminology.Business Component: Discrete business capability or responsibility (example: Delivery Confirmation).
terminology.Implementation Component: Locally created software module implementing or modeling business behavior (example: Frontier.Delivery).
terminology.Integration: Relationship connecting two or more Business Applications for information exchange or coordinated activity.
terminology.Interface: Defined communication boundary exposed or consumed by an application.
terminology.Integration Contract: Data and behavior agreement at an integration boundary.
terminology.Adapter / Connector: Custom code translating between application interfaces/contracts where necessary.
terminology.Integration Service: Executable intermediary performing synchronization, translation, orchestration, retries, or other coordination when required.

rules: Every Implementation Component has exactly one primary parent Business Application in the logical architecture.
An Implementation Component may interact with multiple other Business Applications through Integrations.
Primary logical ownership does not assert code is physically deployed inside a vendor Business Application.
Business Applications may support multiple Business Processes and Business Components.
Integrations connect Business Applications; Interfaces and Contracts specify the boundary; adapters or services implement intermediary custom behavior only where needed.
Do not invent missing Business Applications to satisfy ownership; unresolved ownership stays unresolved pending steward decision.

Test, debug and demonstration outputs must identify relevant Business Application, Business System, Business Process, Business Component, Integration context, and Implementation Component as known; level of detail is deferred.
